prompt: Build Markdown Notebook, a personal notes app that runs as one self-contained HTML page with no server, no build step and no libraries. A tab bar across the top switches between twelve views, one per feature. Notes: create, edit (title and markdown body) and delete notes. Preview: the current note rendered from markdown (headings, bold, italics, inline code, bullet lists, links, paragraphs) with any raw HTML shown as text, never executed. Tags: every #tag written in a note, with the notes that carry it. Links: the [[Title]] links in the current note and whether each target exists. Backlinks: the notes that link to the current one. Search: type words and get the notes containing all of them, title hits first. Outline: the current note's headings as a table of contents. Stats: word count, character count and reading time. Pinned: pinned notes on top, the rest by last update, with a pin toggle. History: undo and redo of every change to the notes. Export / Import: the whole notebook as JSON text, and paste JSON back in. Saved data: everything persists in the browser between visits. Write your own implementation from scratch.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: markdown-notebook.html, one self-contained HTML page. All 14 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The page starts with <!doctype html>, makes zero external requests, holds a <nav> with one button[data-tab=NAME] and one <section id="panel-NAME"> per feature, and one plain <script id="app"> (not a module) that runs to completion in node with document, window and localStorage stubbed and leaves window.App.features holding one entry per feature, each with a `model` object of pure functions and a `render(root, state)` function. The twelve features, each scored by its own test test_feature_NAME: 1. notes: the user creates a note (title, body, unique id, created and updated stamps equal, not pinned), edits its title or body (only that note changes and its updated stamp moves) and deletes it by id; the list the user had is never modified in place. 2. markdown: the preview renders # and ## headings, **bold**, *italics*, `inline code`, - bullet lists, [text](url) links and paragraphs, and shows raw HTML such as <script> as escaped text. 3. tags: every #word in a note is a tag, lower-cased, listed once in order of first appearance; a heading line (# followed by a space) is not a tag; a tag index maps each tag to the ids of the notes carrying it. 4. links: the [[Title]] targets of a note are listed once each in order of appearance, and a title resolves to the id of the note with that title regardless of case, or to null. 5. backlinks: for a note, the ids of the other notes whose body links to its title, case-insensitively. 6. search: the notes containing every whitespace-separated term of the query in title or body, case-insensitive, notes whose title contains the whole query first, each group in list order; an empty or blank query lists everything. 7. outline: the heading lines of a note as {level, text} in document order, level 1 to 6. 8. stats: words (whitespace-separated), characters (the body's length) and reading minutes (words / 200 rounded up, 0 for an empty note). 9. pins: the notes ordered pinned first, then most recently updated first, and a toggle that flips one note's pin without touching the others. 10. history: an undo/redo trail of snapshots: push records a new present and clears redo, undo and redo step through it and are no-ops at either end, canUndo and canRedo say which is possible. 11. exporter: the notebook exports as a JSON object holding a notes array, imports back from that text with ids, titles and bodies intact, and imports nothing from unparseable text or JSON without a notes array. 12. persist: the notes are saved to localStorage as JSON and restored on the next visit; with nothing saved, loading yields null. If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a page that games the tests.
